channel.description: Recent content in Glossary on CCASH — Whitelabel Money Services Platform

item.title: Agent MSB - Glossary
item.description:
Full Definition

An Agent MSB is a legal designation under 31 CFR §1022.380(d) where a business conducts money-services activities on behalf of a principal FinCEN-registered MSB. In the CCASH model, each whitelabel client launches as a Client Series (C-###) designated as an Agent MSB under CCASH's principal FinCEN registration. The Agent MSB operates under its own brand (DBA) while the principal MSB maintains the FinCEN registration, agent list, and AML program oversight. Agents can graduate to their own independent FinCEN registration (Path B — legal graduation).

item.title: AML (Anti-Money Laundering) - Glossary
item.description: AML (Anti-Money Laundering) refers to the laws, regulations, and procedures that prevent criminals from disguising illegally obtained funds as legitimate income. CCASH provides AML compliance infrastructure — transaction monitoring, sanctions screening, and suspicious activity reporting — for every money-services operation money-services operation on the platform.

item.title: Approval Gate - Glossary
item.description: An Approval Gate is a risk-tiered checkpoint that holds a transaction until the required authorization is given. CCASH classifies actions by risk and routes higher-risk ones — large transfers, swaps, travel-cheque redemptions, overrides — through OTP confirmation and, where configured, multi-party approval before they execute. Every gate decision is captured in the signed audit trail.

item.title: Atomic Settlement - Glossary
item.description: Atomic Settlement is the simultaneous exchange of assets and payment in a single transaction — neither side can fail without the other. On CCASH, a Swap applies the quoted FX rate and settles atomically: one balance is debited and the other credited in a single operation. Both legs post to the ledger together or not at all. This eliminates settlement risk — the window where one party has paid but the other has not.

item.title: Audit Trail - Glossary
item.description: An Audit Trail is a chronological record of every action in a system. CCASH provides a cryptographic audit trail for all money-services operation operations — every transaction, governance vote, and configuration change is signed and recorded. The trail is continuous from the shared platform through self-hosted graduation.

item.title: BLOOM - Glossary
item.description: BLOOM is an identity verification specification that CCASH implements for KYC/KYB workflows. It defines a state-machine approach to identity verification where each step is logged and irreversible.

item.title: Broker-Dealer - Glossary
item.description: A Broker-Dealer is a financial intermediary that buys and sells securities on behalf of clients or its own account. Broker-dealers are registered with the SEC and FINRA in the United States. CCASH is not a broker-dealer — it is a money-services platform operated by a FinCEN-registered MSB. Clients who are broker-dealers may use CCASH infrastructure for their money-services operations.

item.title: Cap'n Proto - Glossary
item.description: Cap’n Proto is a zero-copy serialization protocol — data is read directly from the wire format with no encoding or decoding step. CCASH uses Cap’n Proto for inter-grain RPC communication, enabling native Sandstorm integration without an HTTP bridge.

item.title: Capability Security - Glossary
item.description: Capability Security is a model where access is granted through unforgeable tokens (capabilities) rather than identity-based permissions. CCASH uses capability security at every level — from inter-grain communication to user access control — ensuring least-privilege access throughout the platform.

item.title: Compliance - Glossary
item.description: Compliance means adhering to the legal and regulatory requirements that apply to your operations. CCASH provides built-in compliance infrastructure — identity verification, transaction monitoring, audit trails, and reporting — for every money-services operation money-services operation on the platform, whether on the shared platform or a self-hosted instance.

item.title: Compliance Framework - Glossary
item.description:
Full Definition

The compliance framework within the CCASH platform consists of policies and procedures covering customer identification and verification, customer due diligence, transaction review, and reporting obligations. The platform provides operator-facing review surfaces for sanctions screening verdicts and transaction monitoring — the screening engine runs in dedicated compliance infrastructure integrated with the platform. These policies form the foundation of the compliance layer and are enforced through the technology platform's governance tooling.

item.title: Corporate Treasury - Glossary
item.description: Corporate Treasury is the management of an organization’s own cash and assets — holding balances across currencies, moving funds, converting via FX, and keeping accurate records. CCASH runs as treasury software: multi-currency wallets, Send/Receive/Swap, FX, multi-party approval gates, and reconciliation give a company controlled, auditable management of its funds, in the same platform an operator uses to serve customers.

item.title: Custody - Glossary
item.description: Custody is the safekeeping of assets on behalf of wallet holders. CCASH provides custody infrastructure through its capability-secured grain architecture, with multi-party controls and cryptographic audit trails. Whether on the shared platform or a self-hosted instance, asset custody follows the same security model.

item.title: Data Sovereignty - Glossary
item.description: Data Sovereignty means that your money-services operation’s data belongs to you and stays under your control. On the shared platform, your data is isolated from other participants. When you graduate to a self-hosted instance, your data transfers completely — no gaps, no copies left behind, no ongoing access by CCASH.

item.title: Entity Compartment - Glossary
item.description:
Full Definition

An entity compartment is a legally separate cell within the CCASH legal infrastructure structure, dedicated to a specific operator. Each compartment maintains its own records, assets, and liabilities, providing legal separation between operators. This structure ensures that the obligations of one operator do not affect the assets or operations of another.

item.title: Entity Framework - Glossary
item.description: The Entity Framework is CCASH’s set of pre-built legal structures — including Series LLC and other entity types — that provide legal isolation between operating compartments while maintaining operational efficiency. The framework is the legal foundation for the shared platform model.

item.title: Escrow - Glossary
item.description: Escrow refers to funds or assets held by a neutral party until specified conditions are met. CCASH supports escrow patterns for money-services operation money-services operations that require conditional releases, milestone-based payments, or dispute resolution mechanisms.

item.title: Fiat Rails - Glossary
item.description: Fiat rails refer to the integration of a money-services operation with traditional payment and settlement infrastructure — correspondent banking, SEPA, SWIFT, ACH, and card networks. The CCASH platform supports operator-configured fiat rails through provider wiring and the Swap (FX) surface, enabling fiat on-ramps, off-ramps, and settlement across the operator’s configured currency set.

item.title: FinCEN - Glossary
item.description:
Full Definition

FinCEN (Financial Crimes Enforcement Network) is a bureau of the US Department of the Treasury that administers the Bank Secrecy Act (BSA). FinCEN regulates Money Services Businesses (MSBs) under 31 CFR §1022.380, requiring registration, AML program implementation, recordkeeping, and reporting of suspicious activity. CCA.SH MONEY SERVICES (US) SERIES LLC is a FinCEN-registered MSB. The CCASH platform's compliance surfaces are designed to support operations conducted under FinCEN-registered MSB structures.

item.title: Four-Eyes Principle - Glossary
item.description:
Full Definition

A governance requirement that certain critical actions must be approved by two distinct authorized signers before execution. Within the CCASH platform, four-eyes applies to high-tier transactions, customer verification final approval, override decisions on flagged items, refunds above threshold, and policy exception approvals. The requirement is enforced through the technology platform's cryptographic signature verification, ensuring that no single individual can authorize sensitive operations.

item.title: Framework Agreement - Glossary
item.description:
Full Definition

A framework agreement is a governing instrument executed at onboarding that establishes the legal terms under which an operator participates in the CCASH platform. It defines the rights, obligations, and operational parameters of the relationship, including provisions for growth, transition, and termination.

item.title: FX Rate - Glossary
item.description: An FX Rate is the price at which one currency or asset is exchanged for another. CCASH applies an FX rate to every Swap and cross-currency payment, sourced and quoted at the time of the transaction. The rate used is recorded with the transaction so the conversion can be reconciled and audited, and operators can configure spreads and rate sources per deployment.

item.title: Governance Framework - Glossary
item.description: A Governance Framework defines how decisions are made within a money-services operation — who can propose changes, how approvals work, and what authority different participants have. CCASH provides governance tooling including role-based access control (7 user roles), multi-party approval for critical operations, and cryptographically signed audit trails. The framework travels with you — from the shared platform through self-hosted graduation.

item.title: Governance Roles - Glossary
item.description:
Full Definition

Governance roles define the responsibilities, authorities, and limitations of each participant within the CCASH platform. The governance framework establishes supervisory roles with defined veto scope covering regulatory safety, intellectual property compliance, and operational integrity. Operational roles handle day-to-day management of services within the boundaries set by the governance framework.

item.title: Graduation Model - Glossary
item.description: The Graduation Model is CCASH’s core value proposition. Start your money-services operation money-services operation on our proven shared infrastructure — no development required, no infrastructure to manage. When your money-services operation grows, you graduate to your own self-hosted CCASH instance. Your brand, your data, your infrastructure. No lock-in, no platform risk. Your money-services operation, operational data, and audit history transfer cleanly.

item.title: Grain - Glossary
item.description: A Grain is the fundamental isolation unit in the Sandstorm/Melusina operating system. Think of it as an indestructible, self-contained process that remembers everything. Each grain has its own append-only journal store, a set of capabilities granted to it, and an independent lifecycle. In CCASH, grains form the building blocks of both the shared platform and self-hosted instances.

item.title: Journal Store - Glossary
item.description: A Journal Store is an append-only encrypted log used by each grain for durable state storage. Every action is recorded in the journal, enabling deterministic replay for audit, forensic analysis, and disaster recovery. The journal is the foundation of CCASH’s tamper-evident audit trail.

item.title: K-Anonymity - Glossary
item.description: K-Anonymity is a privacy principle ensuring that individual data cannot be distinguished from at least k-1 other individuals in a dataset. CCASH applies k-anonymity to protect money-services operation member privacy in aggregate reporting.

item.title: KYC (Know Your Customer) - Glossary
item.description: KYC (Know Your Customer) is the regulatory process of verifying the identity of participants in a financial ecosystem. On CCASH, KYC workflows are built into the platform — whether you’re on the shared platform or a self-hosted instance. Operators configure identity verification requirements for their money-services operation money-services clients based on their specific regulatory obligations and risk profile.

item.title: Ledger - Glossary
item.description: The Ledger is the authoritative record of balances and movements across every wallet on a CCASH deployment. Each Send, Receive, Swap, and travel-cheque action posts double-entry records to the ledger, written append-only to the journal and cryptographically signed. The ledger is the source of truth that reconciliation, reporting, and the audit trail are built on.

item.title: Liquidity - Glossary
item.description: Liquidity refers to the availability of funds to meet payment obligations as they fall due. In money-services operations, liquidity management involves maintaining sufficient balances across currencies and accounts to settle client transactions without delay. CCASH supports liquidity management through multi-currency wallet visibility, FX and swap with atomic settlement, and real-time balance monitoring.

item.title: Melusina - Glossary
item.description: Melusina is the capability-secured operating system and Sandstorm grain runtime that CCASH runs on. Melusina provides OS-level isolation for every component — each grain is a sandboxed application instance with its own journal store, capability set, and security boundary.

item.title: Money Services Business (MSB) - Glossary
item.description:
Full Definition

A Money Services Business (MSB) is a FinCEN-registered business under 31 CFR §1022.380 that provides money transmission, currency exchange, check cashing, money order issuance, stored value, or other money services. Under the CCASH legal infrastructure, a principal MSB (CCA.SH) registers with FinCEN; whitelabel clients launch as a Client Series operating as an Agent MSB under CCASH's registration, with the ability to graduate to their own independent FinCEN registration. The CCASH platform provides the operator-facing tooling to support MSB compliance requirements.

item.title: Multi-Currency Wallet - Glossary
item.description: A Multi-Currency Wallet holds balances in more than one currency or asset class — fiat, stablecoin, and crypto — under a single customer account. On CCASH each wallet supports Send, Receive, and Swap across its balances, with custody, screening, and approval gates applied per transaction. It is the core customer-facing object an operator’s PSP, MSB, and VASP flows act on.

item.title: Multi-Party Control - Glossary
item.description: Multi-Party Control requires more than one authorized person to complete a sensitive action, so no single individual can act alone. On CCASH it backs high-risk approval gates and key operations — large or unusual transfers, configuration changes, and overrides — using four-eyes review and threshold signing. Each participant’s approval is cryptographically signed and recorded in the audit trail.

item.title: On-Chain - Glossary
item.description: On-Chain refers to data or logic that exists on a distributed ledger. CCASH uses on-chain verification mechanisms — cryptographic signatures, authority verification, and audit trails — to enforce rules at the protocol level. Every state-changing audit row carries a cryptographic signature, creating a tamper-evident record that can be independently verified.

item.title: Operating Entity - Glossary
item.description:
Full Definition

An operating entity is a standalone legal entity owned and controlled by an operator within the CCASH platform. It holds the operator's brand, trade names, domains, intellectual property licenses, documentation, and operating manuals. The operating entity structure ensures that operators maintain clear ownership of their brand and operational assets while participating in the CCASH legal framework.

item.title: PDA (Program Derived Address) - Glossary
item.description: A PDA (Program Derived Address) is an address on the Solana blockchain that is deterministically derived from program ID and seed data rather than being associated with a private key. PDAs are used in CCASH for on-chain compliance configuration storage.

item.title: Platform Disclaimer - Glossary
item.description:
Full Definition

CCASH's disclosure principle that all platform services are experimental in nature, carry inherent risk, and may produce unforeseen consequences. All participants must acknowledge these risks before using the CCASH platform. This disclosure ensures that operators and their customers engage with the platform with full awareness of its experimental character.

item.title: Platform Ecosystem - Glossary
item.description:
Full Definition

The platform ecosystem encompasses the complete network of operators, legal infrastructure, technology platform, and governance framework that constitutes CCASH. Operators deploy branded instances of the CCASH technology platform within the legal infrastructure, serving their own customers while benefiting from shared legal and technical foundations. The ecosystem is designed to support multiple operators with strong data isolation and clear role separation.

item.title: Platform User Roles - Glossary
item.description:
Full Definition

Platform user roles define the categories of participants within the CCASH ecosystem. Operators serve end-customers under their own brand, booking customer relationships into entity compartments. Each role carries defined rights, responsibilities, and access levels within the platform's governance framework.

item.title: Powerbox - Glossary
item.description: The Powerbox is CCASH’s inter-grain capability sharing mechanism. Instead of sharing passwords or API keys, grains offer capabilities to each other through the Powerbox. Capabilities are fine-grained, revocable, and auditable — ensuring least-privilege access at every level of a CCASH deployment.

item.title: PSP (Payment Service Provider) - Glossary
item.description: A PSP (Payment Service Provider) moves money on behalf of customers — accepting funds, holding balances, and executing payments. CCASH is whitelabel PSP software: an operator runs Send, Receive, and payout flows over multi-currency wallets, with risk-tiered approval gates, KYC, and a signed audit trail built in. PSP activity sits alongside the platform’s MSB and VASP capabilities for fiat, stablecoin, and crypto.

item.title: Reconciliation - Glossary
item.description: Reconciliation is the process of matching the platform’s ledger against what actually settled on external rails and custody accounts, and resolving any differences. On CCASH ledger postings, settlement instructions, and FX rates give each movement the data needed to reconcile automatically, with exceptions surfaced for review. Reconciliation keeps balances accurate and supports treasury reporting and audit.

item.title: Regulatory Framework - Glossary
item.description: A Regulatory Framework is the body of laws, regulations, and guidelines that govern financial operations. CCASH provides a comprehensive compliance framework that supports money-services operation money-services operations — from the shared platform to self-hosted instances.

item.title: Sandstorm - Glossary
item.description: Sandstorm is the open-source platform for self-hosted web applications that CCASH runs on. Each application runs in a sandboxed grain with its own data store, capability set, and security boundary — providing OS-level isolation for every component.

item.title: Scaling - Glossary
item.description:
Full Definition

Scaling refers to the process of growing an operation on the CCASH platform from initial deployment to full-scale operation. As operators grow their customer base, transaction volume, and operational footprint, they can expand their use of the CCASH legal infrastructure and technology platform. The platform is designed to accommodate growth without requiring operators to rebuild their infrastructure.

item.title: Self-Hosted - Glossary
item.description: Self-hosted means running your own CCASH instance on your own infrastructure after graduating from the shared platform. Your brand, your data, your terms. No ongoing platform fees, no third-party dependency. The same CCASH platform you started with, now under your complete control. This is the destination of the graduation journey.

item.title: Series LLC - Glossary
item.description:
Full Definition

A limited liability company structure that allows the creation of legally separate compartments within a single LLC. Each compartment has its own assets, liabilities, and purposes, providing legal separation between different operations. This structure forms the foundation of the CCASH legal infrastructure, enabling multiple operators to maintain segregated operations within a unified framework.

item.title: Series LLC - Glossary
item.description: A Series LLC is a corporate structure that allows multiple segregated series to operate under a single LLC umbrella. Each series has its own assets, liabilities, and members — providing legal isolation while maintaining operational efficiency. This structure is the legal foundation for CCASH’s shared platform model.

item.title: Settlement Instructions - Glossary
item.description: Settlement Instructions are the details that tell the platform how and where to move funds to complete a payment — the paying and receiving accounts or wallets, currency, amount, rail, and any references. On CCASH each Send, Swap, or payout carries settlement instructions that drive the ledger postings and feed reconciliation, so every movement can be matched against what actually settled.

item.title: Shared Platform - Glossary
item.description: The Shared Platform is CCASH’s operator infrastructure where money-services businesses launch as a Client Series (C-###) before they graduate to self-hosted instances. It provides compliance surfaces and technology infrastructure — one grain per client — meaning you can launch your operation in weeks, not months, without building infrastructure yourself. Each client operates under CCASH’s US FinCEN MSB registration as an Agent MSB, with the path to graduate to their own self-hosted instance (Path A) or own license (Path B).

item.title: Signed Writes - Glossary
item.description: Signed Writes mean every state-changing action is cryptographically signed (Ed25519) before it is committed. On CCASH each ledger posting, approval, and configuration change is signed by the authority that initiated it and appended to the journal, producing a tamper-evident record. This makes the audit trail provable: who did what, when, and under whose authority.

item.title: Site Profile - Glossary
item.description: A Site Profile is the per-operator configuration that defines a whitelabel deployment: brand and domain, enabled features (Send/Receive/Swap, travel cheques), supported currencies and FX sources, risk tiers and approval-gate thresholds, and KYC settings. On the shared platform each Client Series has its own site profile, isolated from others, and the same profile carries over when an operator graduates to a self-hosted instance.

item.title: Smart Contract - Glossary
item.description: A Smart Contract is self-executing code that automatically enforces the rules of an agreement. In the CCASH ecosystem, programmatic rules handle transaction compliance checks — sanctions screening, velocity limits, and approval gates — before any money movement executes. Compliance rules are encoded so violations are structurally impossible rather than caught after the fact.

item.title: SPV (Special Purpose Vehicle) - Glossary
item.description: An SPV (Special Purpose Vehicle) is a separate legal entity created to isolate financial risk and hold specific assets separate from a parent. CCASH uses Series LLC architecture as a flexible alternative to traditional SPVs, providing legal isolation without the overhead of separate entity formation.

item.title: Swap - Glossary
item.description: Swap is the in-wallet exchange of one currency or asset for another — fiat to stablecoin, crypto to fiat, or between currencies. On CCASH a Swap applies the quoted FX rate and settles atomically, debiting one balance and crediting the other in a single operation, with screening and approval gates applied by risk tier. Both legs are posted to the ledger and signed into the audit trail.

item.title: Tenant Isolation - Glossary
item.description: Tenant Isolation keeps each operator’s data, balances, and configuration separate on the shared platform, so one tenant cannot see or affect another. CCASH enforces this through capability-secured grains and per-tenant journals: every operation is scoped to its own tenant by construction. Isolation underpins whitelabel hosting and makes graduation to a dedicated self-hosted instance a clean handover.

item.title: Threshold Signing - Glossary
item.description: Threshold Signing is a cryptographic scheme where a minimum number of independent signers must cooperate to produce a valid signature. No single party can act alone. CCASH uses threshold signing for high-authority operations — Master NFT control, governance decisions, and critical system parameters.

item.title: Travel Cheque - Glossary
item.description: A Travel Cheque is a prepaid, redeemable instrument an operator can issue and later honor for value. On CCASH a customer can buy a travel cheque from a wallet balance and redeem it later; issuance and redemption pass through risk-tiered approval gates and screening, post to the ledger, and are recorded in the signed audit trail. Buy and redeem are tracked so outstanding cheques reconcile against issued value.

item.title: Travel Rule - Glossary
item.description: The Travel Rule requires that originator and beneficiary information accompany qualifying funds and virtual-asset transfers between providers. CCASH captures and transmits the required counterparty data on Send and crypto transfers, ties it to KYC records, and logs it in the signed audit trail — so an operator running MSB, PSP, and VASP flows can meet travel-rule obligations as part of normal money movement.

item.title: Treasury Series - Glossary
item.description: A Treasury Series is a legal compartment within a Series LLC structure dedicated to managing treasury assets. In the CCASH ecosystem, treasury series can hold and manage the proceeds of money-services operations, providing legal isolation and clear audit trails.

item.title: Trustee - Glossary
item.description: A Trustee is an independent party who oversees compliance with governing documents and acts in participants’ interests. In the CCASH ecosystem, trustees can be configured as part of the governance framework for money-services operations that require independent oversight.

item.title: VASP (Virtual Asset Service Provider) - Glossary
item.description: A VASP (Virtual Asset Service Provider) handles crypto and stablecoin on behalf of customers — exchange, transfer, and custody of digital assets. CCASH provides the VASP software an operator needs to run those flows: crypto and stablecoin wallets, Swap, on-chain transfer hooks, sanctions screening, and travel-rule data capture, all recorded in the signed audit trail. VASP capabilities run together with the platform’s MSB and PSP money-movement features.

item.title: Waterfall - Glossary
item.description: A Waterfall is the order in which proceeds from a money-services operation are distributed among participants. CCASH supports programmable waterfalls through smart contracts — automating distribution according to rules defined by the money-services operation creator.

item.title: White-Label - Glossary
item.description: White-Label refers to operating a CCASH platform under your own brand. On the shared platform, your money-services operation sees your brand while CCASH provides the infrastructure. When you graduate to self-hosted, your brand operates on your own infrastructure. Your money-services operation never needs to know about CCASH unless you choose to tell them.

item.title: Whitelabel Oversight - Glossary
item.description: Whitelabel Oversight is the supervision CCASH retains over operators running on the shared platform under its US FinCEN MSB registration. While a Client Series operates as an Agent MSB under its own brand, CCASH monitors compliance posture, approval-gate activity, and the signed audit trail across tenants. Oversight applies until an operator graduates to a self-hosted instance or its own license, after which it operates independently.
